summary:
Independent review of pacing-int (HEAD 5fc0e06) against spec.md. I read the full src diff c0f21d5..HEAD (director, MonitoringState, common, CameraFeeds, channels/anomalies/props/Figure, ControlRoom, OSD, sfx, script.js) and built my own copy at /tmp/rev-code/game.html. I ran the node sim (200 runs per persona; all assertions pass) and three browser probes, all with zero console errors:
- /tmp/rev-code/t1.js: prologue→monitoring OSD clock, lock gate with a pause, alert mashing, offscreen draw calls and shader programs for every stage.
- /tmp/rev-code/act.js: a whole autopilot act at speed 4 with a post-limiter audio meter and an in-page blind-spot watcher.
- /tmp/rev-code/t2.js: a ?clock=02:11 direct start, a reset to PROLOGUE (same path as the loop), then loop-2 lock gate and first alert.

The core systems are solid:
- The director, blind-spot guard, epoch guards, loop-reset cleanup, fastForward, shader precompile and audio all behave as specified.
- Every stage change in the act happened off-screen and unobserved.

I found one real regression: the CAM-03 OSD clock runs backwards (02:00:59 → 02:00:01) at the PROLOGUE→MONITORING handover. This breaks the spec's "seconds never run backwards" invariant and adds an unintended time anomaly on the main screen. There are two minor spec deviations: the second knock set ignores open inspects, and ?pace=0 is not quite "today's build". No blockers.
verifiedOk: pacing-sim (200 runs per persona, all assertions pass): typical 4:22/4:27/4:33, eager 3:58/4:00/4:02, starer 5:01, passive 5:23; figure 7 at the end and the knock in 02:05 in every run. Its claims hold in the code: protected minutes flip only at e ≥ SPM (canFlip); MIN_GAP is enforced in _tickFire and only fire() (debug) bypasses it; the CAM-03 alarm is cancelled when seen, observed, held, within POST_HOLD or after ventStopped; tones never play while held or after ventStopped. One relaxation: the sim checks max idle as median ≤ 21.5 s with a hard cap of 24 s, not spec §9.1's ≤ 21 s. Its header explains why.

Whole autopilot act (/tmp/rev-code/act.json, speed 4, seed 7): 268.8 s game time, figure 7, 8 cued alerts, 11 applies, 1 CAM-03 alarm and 8 cancelled. The in-page watcher (30 ms sampling) saw 9 stage changes, all with shown=false and observed=false. No trace 'apply' entry hit a shown channel. The knock fired in minute 5 with the figure at index 4.

Audio, whole act post-limiter: peak −16.0 dBFS, largest 50 ms RMS −22.4 dBFS (≤ −10 rule holds). In context with the ambience, vmdTone reads −27.0 to −29.5 dBFS (the integrator already flagged the −27 reading) and doorKnock −28.3 / −28.6 dBFS. The lock-gate lever and unlatch at the door read −18.3 to −21.9 dBFS.

Shader programs stay at 89 when every stage of every channel is rendered offscreen, so no compiles mid-play. Draw calls per stage at 160×120:
- CAM-01: 29 / 29 / 31
- CAM-02: 29 / 36 / 40 / 45 / 47
- CAM-03: 58 / 64
- CAM-04: 42 / 41 / 52
These match the spec's estimates, and only the shown channel renders.
Alert mashing: 24 rapid CAM button presses during the m4a alert produced no apply on a shown channel. OSD tag and alarm-line latching were correct, and both CAM-04 and CAM-03 acked normally.

Lock gate: the right screen goes normalUnlocked → normal, the objective goes lockDoor → monitor, and the SYS LOG gets '02:00 防爆門 手動上鎖（操作員）'. Pausing mid-animation held blastLocking with no completion, and it finished after resume. The wheel ends at −2.5π and the bolts at 0, so openBlastDoor in the ending starts from the right bolt position.
?clock=02:11 direct start: stages [2,3,1,2], CAM-04 frozen OSD shows 02:14:08 when switched in, all 11 fastForward SYS LOG lines present and sorted, doorKnocked=true, door locked.

Reset to PROLOGUE (the same applyPreset→resetWorld path the loop uses) clears everything: stages, alerts, alert levels, frozen time, tag, figureSub, logExtra, minuteK, director alias and trail; the door is unlocked and the right screen reads normalUnlocked. In loop 2 the lock gate, the first CAM-04 alert (01:58:41) and the SYS LOG all work.

Epoch safety: all new waits, untils and bus handlers go through BaseState guards, and exit() clears lockPending, blastLocking, minuteK, the director and the alerts. Director tick and handler exceptions are caught. All new meshes and materials are created at construction time. Only intensity, opacity, colour, fog and map swaps happen at runtime, and the light count is unchanged.
Copy: every new string matches spec §5 and is marked 【補充文案】. The only edits to existing text are the two 02:11 → 02:05 corrections, both of them in 【補充文案】 strings, so no 【原企劃文案】 text changed.

LED comfort by code: the cam LED breathes 0.85–1.0 over 2.4 s (15%) and stays steady at 0.8 under reduceFlicker. The blast lamp while locking breathes 15% over 1.4 s and is steady under reduceFlicker. AGC × meanScale math gives a worst-case switch of about 15% per 0.25 s (CAM-04 → CAM-01 stage 2, agcFrom ≈ 2.5, smoothstep over 2 s).

findings.title: CAM-03 OSD clock jumps backwards (02:00:59 → 02:00:00) when MONITORING starts after the prologue
findings.detail:
During the prologue minuteK is null, so CameraFeeds._timestamp uses the old formula and the main CRT's OSD counts 02:00:00 → 02:00:59 and holds there; the prologue usually lasts more than 17 s. On MonitoringState.enter the director's onMinute(0) publishes minuteK = 0. The clock text is still '02:00', but _kStale is cleared because k < 0.5, so the OSD jumps back to 02:00:00 and counts up again through the lock-gate minute.

This breaks spec §4 'Seconds never run backwards' and the docs, which claim the same (DESIGN-NOTES E2: 秒數永不倒退). It also adds an unplanned, visible time anomaly on CAM-03, the screen the player has just been staring at. The spec treats the CAM-04 02:14:08 freeze as the only time anomaly.

Scope:
- Happens on every loop and with ?lock=0.
- Does not happen with ?pace=0, so the owner's A/B comparison will show it only in the new build.
findings.evidence: /tmp/rev-code/t1.js part A (output in /tmp/rev-code/t1.json, key A). Last prologue samples: time '02:00:59', minuteK null. First MONITORING samples: '02:00:59' (k=0), then '02:00:01', '02:00:02', … '02:00:12'. Code: src/world/CameraFeeds.js:502-515 (_timestamp: the _kStale/minuteK branch has no lower bound for an unchanged clock text); src/states/monitoringDirector.js onMinute() sets k=0 and io.minuteK(0); MonitoringState.run calls onMinute(0) on natural entry.
findings.suggestedFix:
Make the OSD seconds monotonic for an unchanged clock text. In CameraFeeds._timestamp, keep this._secFloor and reset it to 0 when `text !== this._clockText`. Otherwise return `max(sec, this._secFloor)` and update the floor. After a long prologue, minute 0 then holds :59 until 02:01, exactly as in ?pace=0.

Alternative: on natural entry, seed minute 0 from the displayed seconds. Set `minuteT0 = now - (sec0/60)·SPM` and `k = sec0/60` right after director.onMinute(0).

findings.title: Second knock set (+2.4 s) plays even while an inspect or a hold is open
findings.detail:
_tickKnock checks held, inspectOpen and door distance before the first set. At step 2 it re-checks only door distance, so if the player opens an inspect (desk items: coffee, notes) within the 2.4 s gap, the second set plays over the close-up.

Spec §3.6 and §8 say the knock is never played during an inspect. The sound is soft (≈ −28.5 dBFS), so this is polish, not a scare.
findings.evidence: src/states/monitoringDirector.js:448-455: the `kn.step === 1` branch tests only `playerDoorDist >= minDoorDist` before `io.knock(2, 0.8)`. Compare lines 433-438, where the armed state checks `s.held || s.inspectOpen`.
findings.suggestedFix: At step 2, also require `!s.held && !s.inspectOpen`. If either holds, either skip the set (trace 'knockQuiet', as the door-distance branch already does) or defer it by at most ~1 s and then skip.

findings.title: ?pace=0 still shows new feed content (CAM-03 wet trail grows with the figure, plus new stage-0 baseline props)
findings.detail:
The owner play-test (spec §9.5, STATUS step 1) compares the defaults against ?pace=0, described as 'today's build'. README and DESIGN-NOTES E4 describe it as 改版前的流程 (the pre-redesign flow).

However, installAnomalies always runs, and Cam03.setFigurePose extends the trail on every index change whatever the pace flags say. In ?pace=0 the CAM-03 trail therefore still appears at index ≥ 2 and lengthens with each step. The always-on stage-0 baseline is also visible: the CAM-01 LD gantry with 1.35× signs and the CAM-04 dome glow. The 02:11 → 02:05 copy retime applies in both modes too.

This muddies the A/B comparison, especially question 3 ('is CAM-03 change frequency right?').
findings.evidence: src/world/feeds/channels.js:516-522: the trail.reach() update has no pace check. src/world/feeds/channels.js createChannels() calls installAnomalies() unconditionally. src/states/common.js paceFlags() only gates director, lock, subposes and the knock. Docs: docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md:150, README.md:34.
findings.suggestedFix:
Either:
- add a `feeds.anomaliesOn` flag (set from paceFlags(ctx).pace in resetWorld and MonitoringState.enter, like subPoses) and make Cam03.setFigurePose call trail.reach(null) when it is off, optionally hiding the CAM-04 dome glow as well; or
- document in DESIGN-NOTES E4 and README that ?pace=0 keeps the trail and the stage-0 baseline props, so the owner knows what is being compared.
